args.summary:
Decision written to review/A-dashboard-5/decision.json: PROMOTE.

Evidence from the dashboard:
- Zero 5xx on both arms, overall and per-route (stable 0/7343, canary 0/2476; err% 0.00% everywhere). No correctness or availability signal against the canary.
- Aggregate canary latency looks worse (p95 177ms vs 94ms, p99 218ms vs 104ms), and the same gap appears on every route (/browse 150 vs 27, /search 177 vs 59, /checkout 215 vs 103).
- The over-time breakdown explains that gap: canary p95 was 210ms in 0-30s, 130ms in 30-60s, then 95ms in 60-90s and 94ms in 90-120s, against a flat stable p95 of 93-95ms. The canary converges to parity with stable in the second half of the test.
- Judgement: the aggregate p95/p99 are inflated by the first ~60s only; this is the signature of a cold start (empty caches / JIT / connection pool warmup) on a single freshly-started pod, not a sustained performance regression. The last 60s — half the test — shows the canary indistinguishable from stable.

Risk note (judgement): the canary is a single pod with only 514 /checkout requests, so a rare or load-dependent fault could hide below that sample size, and the warmup penalty will recur on each pod as it rolls. Recommended follow-up is to promote with a staged rollout and watch p95 plus 5xx on /checkout through the first minutes of each new pod, rather than treating promote as the end of the observation window.
